facts.statement: Yamatosaurus is a basal hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous found on Awaji Island in Japan.
facts.quote: Yamatosaurus (meaning "Yamato reptile") is a genus of basal hadrosaurid from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)-aged Kita-Ama Formation of Awaji Island, Japan.

facts.statement: The genus Yamatosaurus contains only one known species, Yamatosaurus izanagii.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Yamatosaurus izanagii.

facts.statement: Shingo Kishimoto discovered the holotype of Yamatosaurus on Awaji Island in Japan in May 2004.
facts.quote: The holotype MNHAH D1-033516, consisting of part of the right lower jaw, twelve teeth, four cervical vertebrae, three cervical ribs, a partial right coracoid and a posterior caudal vertebra, was discovered on Awaji Island in Japan in May 2004 by Shingo Kishimoto.

facts.statement: The discovery of Yamatosaurus was first reported in scientific literature in 2005.
facts.quote: In 2005, the find was reported in the scientific literature.

facts.statement: The holotype was donated to a museum in Hyogo Prefecture in 2013 and formally described in 2021 after preparation by Kazumi Wada, Tomomi Ikeda, and Chisato Ota.
facts.quote: Kishimoto in 2013 donated the holotype to Japan's Museum of Nature and Human Activities in the Hyogo Prefecture, where the fossils were prepared by Kazumi Wada, Tomomi Ikeda and Chisato Ota to be described in 2021.

facts.statement: Yamatosaurus izanagii was named in 2021 by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Ryuji Takasaki, Katsuhiro Kubota, and Anthony Ricardo Fiorillo.
facts.quote: The species Yamatosaurus izanagii was named in 2021 by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Ryuji Takasaki, Katsuhiro Kubota and Anthony Ricardo Fiorillo.

facts.statement: Yamatosaurus lived during the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 71.94 to 71.69 million years ago.
facts.quote: The sediments date to subchron 32.1r28, corresponding to the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, around 71.94–71.69 million years ago, making it roughly contemporaneous with fellow Japanese hadrosaur Kamuysaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Yamatosaurus were found in marine sediments deposited on the edge of a continental slope in an intra-arc basin.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in dark grey mudstones within the upper part Kita-Ama Formation, which was deposited in marine conditions in distal turbidite facies on the edge of the continental slope in an intra-arc basin.

facts.statement: Yamatosaurus is classified as a basal hadrosaurid, positioned phylogenetically between Hadrosaurus and the Saurolophinae+Lambeosaurinae clades.
facts.quote: Yamatosaurus is a basal hadrosaurid, more derived than Hadrosaurus but less than Saurolophinae+Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Yamatosaurus coexisting with the more derived Kamuysaurus indicates a level of provinciality in hadrosaur evolution.
facts.quote: However, it was also contemporaneous with the more derived Kamuysaurus, suggesting some level of provinciality.

facts.statement: Yamatosaurus belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
Yamatosaurus is a member of the family Hadrosauridae.
The genus Yamatosaurus was established by Kobayashi et al. in 2021.
Yamatosaurus izanagii lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 71 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Yamatosaurus izanagii es la única especie conocida del género Yamatosaurus ("lagarto de Yamato") de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido basal que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 71 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiano, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Yamatosaurus is a basal hadrosaurid that is more derived than Hadrosaurus but less derived than Saurolophinae and Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Yamatosaurus es un hadrosáurido basal, más derivado que Hadrosaurus pero menos que los Saurolophinae+Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: The time range for the genus Yamatosaurus is estimated from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The presence of Yamatosaurus suggests that East Asia may have served as a refuge for basal hadrosaurs during the Late Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Its presence, along with those of Plesiohadros and Tanius, suggests East Asia may have served as a refuge for basal hadrosaurs in the Late Cretaceous.
